## Best Fabric for Embroidery: Cotton, Polo Piqué, Fleece, Nylon Explained
URL: https://lakesidethreadz.com/blog/best-fabric-for-embroidery/

Q: Does polyester embroider well?
A: Medium-weight polyester (performance polos, athletic pullovers) embroiders cleanly with proper backing. Thin polyester (lightweight athletic tees) can pucker — ask us for a sample press before committing to a big run.

Q: Can you embroider on a dress shirt?
A: Yes, but we usually recommend keeping the design small (left-chest or cuff) and simple on dress shirts. Dense full-back embroidery on a fine oxford fabric can warp the shirt.

Q: Will embroidery make a thin t-shirt look wavy?
A: Possible with very dense designs on light cotton. For t-shirt embroidery we usually suggest a smaller logo (2.5 inches or less) or switching to a heavier shirt (Champion T525C) to avoid the puckered look.

Q: Can you embroider on terry cloth towels?
A: Yes — towels embroider beautifully. We use a water-soluble topper to prevent stitches from sinking into the terry loops, and the result looks crisp and lasts the life of the towel.

Q: What about leather or faux leather patches?
A: Real leather patches (sewn onto hats or jackets) embroider cleanly. Faux leather we do too but the needle holes can be slightly visible. For leather patches on hats, most customers prefer a laser-engraved patch and we can source that.

## Custom Shirts No Minimum Order: How Single-Piece Printing Works
URL: https://lakesidethreadz.com/blog/custom-shirts-no-minimum-order/

Q: What's the minimum order at Lakeside Ink & Threadz?
A: No minimum. We'll do one t-shirt, one polo, one hat, one hoodie. Tier pricing starts getting meaningfully better at 12 pieces and keeps improving through 48 and 96.

Q: Is there a setup fee for a single shirt?
A: For DTF printing (full-color prints): no setup fee. For embroidery: there's a one-time $25-50 digitizing fee if we're converting your logo to embroidery for the first time. After the first embroidery order, reorders have zero setup.

Q: How long does one custom shirt take to make?
A: Typically 5-7 business days from quote approval. Rush orders (2-3 days) are available for an extra 25%. Walk-in same-day isn't something we do routinely but is occasionally possible if we're not slammed.

Q: Is one custom shirt really cheaper with DTF than screen printing?
A: Yes — because DTF has no per-color setup fee. For a single full-color shirt, DTF is almost always the cheapest method. Screen printing becomes cheaper per piece at roughly 25+ pieces of the same design.

Q: Can I get one custom embroidered polo with my company logo?
A: Yes. First-time logo: expect $25-50 digitizing fee + the per-piece embroidery cost ($14-22 on a mid-tier polo). Second and future orders of the same logo: just the per-piece embroidery cost, no setup.

Q: Do you ship single shirts?
A: Yes — USPS Priority Mail typically $8-12 within Texas, 2-3 days. UPS Ground for larger orders. Free pickup at our Twin Creeks Drive location in Livingston.

## DTF vs Screen Printing vs Embroidery: Which to Choose (2026)
URL: https://lakesidethreadz.com/blog/dtf-vs-screen-printing-vs-embroidery/

Q: Which is cheapest at 24 pieces?
A: For simple 1-color designs: screen printing usually wins at 24 pieces of simple cotton tees. For full-color or non-cotton: DTF beats screen printing because screen has per-color setup fees that don't amortize well at 24. For logos on polos/hats: embroidery almost always wins regardless of quantity.

Q: Which lasts the longest in the wash?
A: Embroidery (it's thread, lasts the life of the garment). Second: properly cured screen printing (50+ washes easily). Third: DTF (40-60 washes with proper care). All three are 'commercial-grade' durable.

Q: Can I do embroidery on a hoodie?
A: Yes — Bella+Canvas 3719 sponge fleece and heavier hoodies embroider beautifully. Avoid dense full-chest embroidery on light-weight hoodies (they'll pucker). Left-chest 3-4 inch logos are the sweet spot.

Q: Is screen printing dead since DTF came along?
A: No — screen printing is still cheaper per piece at 50+ pieces of simple designs, and water-based screen prints feel softer than DTF. Shops increasingly offer both and pick the right one per job.

Q: What's the best method for a photo on a t-shirt?
A: DTF (or DTG if the shop has it and you prioritize softness). Neither screen printing nor embroidery can reproduce photographic detail. DTF handles full-color photos cleanly in one pass.

## DTG vs DTF Printing: Which to Pick for Custom Shirts
URL: https://lakesidethreadz.com/blog/dtg-vs-dtf-printing/

Q: Is DTG or DTF cheaper?
A: Close at single-piece quantities. DTF gets cheaper per piece faster as quantity grows because the transfer production step is more efficient than per-shirt inkjet time.

Q: Does DTG wash out faster than DTF?
A: Slightly, in our testing — DTG shows noticeable fade at 30-40 washes, DTF holds strong to 50-60. Both are acceptable for commercial use with proper care (cold wash, inside out, air dry when possible).

Q: Can DTG print on polyester?
A: Technically yes, but the color saturation and durability are worse than DTF or sublimation on polyester. If your shirt is a performance poly blend or 100% polyester, pick DTF or sublimation.

Q: Is DTG the same as screen printing?
A: No. Screen printing uses physical screens and plastisol or water-based ink; one screen per color. DTG uses a digital inkjet sprayer; no screens, no per-color setup. DTG is the inkjet of garment printing.

Q: Can I feel the DTF print through the shirt?
A: Yes, slightly — run your finger over it and you'll feel a rubbery texture. It's much less than iron-on vinyl or old-school screen printing plastisol. Most customers don't notice unless they're specifically looking for it.

## Embroidery Stitch Count Estimator: Formula + Examples
URL: https://lakesidethreadz.com/blog/embroidery-stitch-count-estimator/

Q: Is higher stitch count always worse?
A: Not necessarily — higher stitch count means more detail and a more premium look. It just costs more per piece. For a founder/executive polo program where piece-by-piece appearance matters, pay for the detail. For a 500-piece event shirt run where cost matters, simplify the design.

Q: Can you reduce stitch count on a logo I already have?
A: Yes. We can re-digitize with a tighter fill pattern, remove 3D puff effects, simplify borders, or convert solid fills to outlines. Expect 20-40% stitch reduction with minimal visual impact if your logo has solid-fill areas.

Q: Why does my logo have different stitch counts at different shops?
A: Because every digitizer makes different choices about underlay, fill density, pull compensation, and stitch direction. A good digitizer optimizes for both appearance and efficiency; a lazy one maxes out density to be safe, inflating stitch count. Ask to see the stitch count before production.

Q: Does stitch count affect how durable the embroidery is?
A: Up to a point, yes. Too few stitches = thin, see-through embroidery that frays. Too many stitches on light fabric = puckering and thread breakage. A well-digitized logo hits the sweet spot — dense enough to look solid, not so dense it warps the garment.

Q: Can you quote me based on stitch count alone?
A: Almost. We need to know the garment type too (polo vs hoodie vs hat), the position (left chest vs full back), and the quantity. With those four variables we can quote within a dollar or two per piece before seeing the final digitized file.

## Embroidery vs Screen Printing: Which to Pick for Custom Apparel
URL: https://lakesidethreadz.com/blog/embroidery-vs-screen-printing/

Q: Is embroidery more expensive than screen printing?
A: Per-piece at low quantities (1-25), they're often close or embroidery is cheaper (because screen has per-color setup fees). At 100+ pieces of a simple 1-2 color design, screen printing is cheaper per piece. The exact break-even depends on your design's stitch count and color count.

Q: Does embroidery damage the fabric?
A: No — embroidery is a sewing process, not a cutting process. The needle passes through the fabric; it doesn't tear. Properly digitized embroidery on quality fabric will outlast the garment.

Q: Can you embroider on a t-shirt?
A: Yes, but we usually recommend a polo, henley, or ringspun cotton tee for embroidery — the thicker fabric handles the stitch weight better. Light cotton tees can pucker around dense embroidery designs.

Q: Does screen printing crack over time?
A: Not if it's cured properly. Cracking usually means the print wasn't fully cured during production, or the shirt was washed hot and tumble-dried hot repeatedly. A properly cured screen print survives 50+ washes easily.

Q: Which one lasts longer?
A: Both last the life of the garment when done well. Embroidery has a slight edge because thread is a physical fiber bonded to the fabric, whereas screen-print ink is a surface layer. But either one typically outlasts the shirt.

## DTF Gang Sheets Explained: How to Save Money on Custom Prints
URL: https://lakesidethreadz.com/blog/gang-sheet-dtf-printing/

Q: Can I buy just the gang sheet of transfers without shirts?
A: Not from Lakeside — we press and ship finished shirts, not loose transfers. Several national vendors (DTFTransfers, UnlimitedDTF, etc.) sell transfer-only gang sheets if you have your own heat press.

Q: How many designs can I fit on a 22x24 gang sheet?
A: Depends on design size. Small 2-inch left-chest logos: 40-50. Medium 4-inch designs: 15-20. Large 8-10 inch chest designs: 4-6. One 12-inch design: 1.

Q: Does gang-sheet print quality differ from a single-design print?
A: No — the printing quality is identical. Each design on the sheet is printed at the same resolution and color accuracy as a single-design sheet.

Q: How do I cut designs off a gang sheet?
A: Kiss-cut with scissors around the outline of each design, leaving 0.125 inches of clear film around the printed area. Don't cut right to the ink edge — you need a bit of film for the adhesive to bond under.

Q: Are gang-sheet transfers as durable as single-design transfers?
A: Yes — same film, same adhesive, same curing process. Durability is identical.

## Custom Embroidery Cost in 2026: Real Prices by Garment
URL: https://lakesidethreadz.com/blog/how-much-does-custom-embroidery-cost/

Q: Is there a minimum order amount?
A: At Lakeside, no. We'll embroider a single polo. Tier pricing starts getting meaningfully better at 12 pieces. For most shops, minimums range from 1-24 pieces.

Q: How is embroidery priced vs screen printing cost-wise?
A: At small quantities (1-24), embroidery and screen printing are close, with embroidery often cheaper because screen has per-color setup fees. At 50+ pieces of a simple 1-2 color design, screen printing is cheaper per piece. For logos on polos or hats, embroidery wins regardless of quantity.

Q: Why does one shop quote me $15 and another $25 for the same shirt?
A: Three common reasons: different blank garments (same style, different brand or weight), different stitch counts (one shop's digitizer added more density), or different overhead structures (large shops have higher fixed costs). Ask each shop for a written quote that itemizes blank cost + embroidery cost + digitizing fee separately.

Q: Does Lakeside charge a setup fee?
A: No setup fee per run. We charge a one-time digitizing fee ($25-50) if you're bringing a new logo. All future reorders of that logo have zero setup cost.

Q: Can I get a real quote same day?
A: Yes. Text or email us a photo of your logo, garment type, quantity, and ideal delivery date. Kristen usually quotes same-day; always within one business day.

## Polo vs T-Shirt for Work Uniforms: Which to Pick
URL: https://lakesidethreadz.com/blog/polo-vs-t-shirt-for-work/

Q: Are polos really more professional than t-shirts?
A: In a customer-facing context, yes — business and consumer surveys consistently rank polos as 'more professional' than t-shirts by 20-30 points. The collar is the visual cue; it reads 'uniform' instead of 'casual.' In contexts where everyone wears a t-shirt (jobsites, warehouses), the professionalism bump disappears.

Q: What's the lifespan difference between a polo and a t-shirt?
A: A good polo (Core 365, Port Authority) lasts 2-3 years of daily wear before fading or wearing out at the collar. A good t-shirt (Bella+Canvas 3001) lasts 1-2 years. Both significantly longer if worn only occasionally.

Q: Can we embroider our logo on a t-shirt?
A: Yes — but the look is less tailored than embroidery on a polo. If you're going embroidery, we usually recommend a ringspun heavy cotton tee (Champion T525C) rather than a light jersey (Bella 3001) because the thicker fabric handles the stitch weight without puckering.

Q: Which is better for summer in Texas?
A: T-shirts breathe better in extreme heat because they have no collar and typically lighter fabric. A moisture-wicking performance polo (Core 365 88181) comes close and keeps the professional look. For outdoor crews in July heat, prioritize breathability over formality.

Q: How many polos or t-shirts should we order per person?
A: For 5-day-a-week wear: 5-7 pieces per person so laundry doesn't become a daily chore. For occasional wear (events, meetings): 2-3 pieces. Reorder annually before fading becomes visible.

## Spirit Wear Fundraiser Guide: Playbook for Booster Clubs
URL: https://lakesidethreadz.com/blog/spirit-wear-fundraiser-guide/

Q: How much does a typical booster spirit wear fundraiser raise?
A: Varies by school size. Small schools (under 500 students, athletic boosters only): $800-2,500 per run. Mid-sized (500-1,500 students): $2,500-6,000. Large (1,500+): $6,000-15,000. Band and Project Grad fundraisers scale similarly.

Q: Do we need to buy inventory in advance?
A: No — the modern approach is pre-order only. Parents order through a Google Form or similar; you place one bulk order with the vendor after the window closes; the booster has zero inventory risk.

Q: What if parents want sizes we didn't order?
A: Build the form to let families select from all adult + youth sizes. The vendor orders exactly what pre-sold. Don't try to predict size distribution — let parents do it.

Q: How long from ordering window close to pickup night?
A: Typically 2-3 weeks for production + packing. Add a week for shipping to the booster president. Schedule the pickup night at least 4 weeks after the ordering window closes.

Q: Can families order individually and have it shipped to them?
A: Possible but more complex. Most booster clubs batch-ship to the president and do a single pickup night; parents who miss pickup night get theirs at a backup pickup the following week. Individual shipping adds per-piece shipping cost and reduces the booster's margin.

Q: How do we handle the school logo approval?
A: Most Texas districts require written vendor approval for the licensed mark. An email from your district's communications or athletics office is usually enough. If you're not sure who to ask, we'll help — we've done this with 10+ Texas schools.

## UV DTF Printing: What It Is and When to Use It
URL: https://lakesidethreadz.com/blog/uv-dtf-printing-explained/

Q: Is UV DTF the same as regular DTF?
A: No — same name, different technology. Regular DTF is for fabric and uses heat + adhesive powder. UV DTF is for hard surfaces and uses UV-cured ink + a peel-and-stick film. Don't mix them up when ordering.

Q: Will UV DTF survive dishwasher and ice-bath use?
A: Yes — properly applied UV DTF on a tumbler survives 100+ dishwasher cycles. Top-rack is safer than bottom-rack for the first few washes while the adhesive fully cures (first 24 hours).

Q: Can I apply UV DTF decals myself at home?
A: Yes, that's actually a huge use case. Many vendors sell loose UV DTF decals and the customer applies them to their own tumblers, phone cases, or laptops. We don't sell loose decals — we press-and-ship complete products.

Q: Does UV DTF work on wood or leather?
A: Not well — those surfaces are too porous for the adhesive to bond properly. For wood, consider laser engraving or vinyl. For leather, consider embroidery or debossing.

Q: How long does UV DTF last outdoors?
A: On cars, water bottles, hard hats — 3-5 years of outdoor exposure with proper application. UV exposure can slowly fade bright colors; apply a clear vinyl laminate over the decal for max weather protection on outdoor surfaces.

## What Is DTF Printing? Direct-to-Film Explained in Plain English
URL: https://lakesidethreadz.com/blog/what-is-dtf-printing/

Q: Is DTF printing the same as DTG (Direct-to-Garment)?
A: No. DTG prints directly onto the fabric using a specialized inkjet — no film, no transfer. DTG is great for 100% cotton at low quantities but has limits (can't print white ink on dark garments as reliably, slower than DTF, higher equipment cost). DTF is a transfer process and works on more fabrics.

Q: How long does a DTF print last on a shirt?
A: A properly pressed DTF print lasts 40-60+ wash cycles with normal care. Wash cold, inside out, air dry if you want to maximize print lifespan. Most customers' shirts outlive the print; some report prints still looking sharp after 100+ washes.

Q: Can DTF be done on dark shirts?
A: Yes — that's actually one of its strongest use cases. The dense white underbase lets full-color designs pop on black, navy, or any dark fabric. Screen printing on dark shirts requires a separate white underbase print, which doubles the setup cost. DTF handles it in one pass.

Q: What's the minimum order for DTF printing?
A: No minimum. We'll run one shirt. One of the main reasons DTF exists is to make low-quantity custom apparel economic — we don't charge screen-setup fees because there are no screens.

Q: Does DTF work on hats, bags, or jackets?
A: Yes on canvas bags, nylon or cotton jackets, polyester performance wear, and heavier canvas pieces. For hats, DTF works on flat-panel foam fronts but is less common — embroidery or heat-transfer vinyl is more typical for hats.

Q: How is DTF different from HTV (iron-on vinyl)?
A: HTV is a single-color plastic vinyl cut into shapes and pressed on. It's cheap and durable but one color per layer and limited to flat shapes. DTF prints photographic full-color detail including fine text and gradients that vinyl can't reproduce.

## Mobile Spray Tanning Onalaska TX | Lakeside Ink & Threadz
URL: https://lakesidethreadz.com/glow/

Q: How long does a spray tan last?
A: A typical spray tan lasts 5-10 days with proper care. Moisturizing daily and avoiding exfoliating products will help extend the life of your tan.

Q: What should I do at least 24 hours before my tan?
A: Exfoliate, exfoliate, exfoliate! 24 hours before your session, use a body scrub to clear away dry, dead skin cells. This ensures even color and long-lasting results. Avoid bar soaps, high-pH shower products, or in-shower moisturizers as these can interfere with the DHA bronzing reaction. Also avoid shaving, waxing, or depilatory creams for at least 24 hours prior.

Q: What should I do the day of my tan?
A: Skip the lotion and makeup — or remove makeup before your session for an even face tan. Use deodorant sparingly (or not at all) as it can interact with the spray and turn your armpits green. Wear loose-fitting, dark cotton clothing and remove all jewelry until your tan is set.

Q: When can I rinse after my spray tan?
A: You have up to 24 hours before your initial rinse. If you feel your tan is dark enough, you can rinse anywhere from 4–24 hours after spraying using lukewarm water only. Do not use shampoos, conditioner, or soaps during the first rinse. This sets the tan and you may see it darken slightly afterward.

Q: How long until I can shower?
A: For regular solution, wait 8-12 hours before your first rinse. If you choose our Rapid Tan add-on, you can shower in just 2-4 hours.

Q: Will the spray tan look orange?
A: Absolutely not! We customize your shade based on your skin tone and desired results. Our premium solutions are designed to give you a natural, golden-bronze glow — never orange.

Q: What if I'm nervous or it's my first time?
A: No worries at all! We guide you through every step of the process. It's quick, painless, and most clients say it's actually relaxing. We'll make sure you're comfortable the entire time.

Q: Do you travel outside the listed service area?
A: Yes! We may be able to accommodate locations outside our standard service area for an additional travel fee. Contact us with your location and we'll let you know.

Q: Can I get a spray tan while pregnant?
A: We recommend consulting with your doctor first. We use pregnancy-safe, DHA-based solutions, but your healthcare provider can best advise based on your individual situation.

Q: How do I book?
A: Use our booking form below or give us a call/text. We typically respond within a few hours and can often accommodate same-week appointments.

Q: What's the proper way to order a three-letter monogram?
A: Give us first, middle, last. If it's the classic style (large center letter), that's traditionally First-LAST-Middle. Different families have different conventions — tell us what order you want and we'll do it exactly.

Q: What's the difference between flat and puff embroidery?
A: Flat embroidery lies smooth against the cap. Puff embroidery uses foam underneath to create a raised 3D effect — popular for bold logos and lettering. Both are durable; it's an aesthetic choice.

## Embroidery Digitizing Onalaska TX | Lakeside Ink & Threadz
URL: https://lakesidethreadz.com/services/embroidery-digitizing/

Q: What is embroidery digitizing?
A: Digitizing converts your logo from an image file into stitch instructions — telling the embroidery machine exactly where to place each stitch, in what order, and with which thread colors.

Q: Why does my logo need to be digitized?
A: Embroidery machines can't read image files directly. They need a specific stitch file format that maps out the thread path. Every logo must be digitized before it can be embroidered.

Q: Do I pay for digitizing every time I order?
A: No. Digitizing is a one-time fee. Once we create your stitch file, we store it and use it for all future orders at no additional digitizing cost.

Q: What file format do you need for my logo?
A: We accept JPG, JPEG, and SVG files. Vector files (SVG, AI, EPS) produce the cleanest results, but we can work with high-resolution images too.

Q: Can you provide just the stitch file without embroidery?
A: Yes. If you have your own embroidery equipment or another provider, we can deliver just the digitized stitch file.

Q: How long does digitizing take?
A: Most logos are digitized within 24-48 hours. Complex designs may take longer. We'll provide a mockup before stitching so you can approve the design.

Q: What is embroidery digitizing?
A: Digitizing converts your logo into a stitch file the embroidery machine can read — telling it where to put each stitch, what thread color, and what density. It's a one-time $45 fee per design and we keep the file on hand for all your future orders.

Q: Why is digitizing a separate cost from the logo design?
A: Because it's a separate craft. A digitizer translates artwork into thousands of individual stitch instructions for the machine. Done well, it determines whether your logo looks crisp or fuzzy on a finished polo, hat, or jacket.

## Services | Custom Embroidery & DTF | L.I.T. Onalaska TX
URL: https://lakesidethreadz.com/services/

Q: How long does embroidery take?

Q: What file do I need to send?

SVG vector files provide the cleanest results at any size. Not sure what you have? Send it anyway — we will let you know if it needs adjustment.

Q: What's the difference between DTF and screen printing?
A: Screen printing is great for large runs of simple designs. DTF is better for detailed art, photos, and small quantities — no setup fees, no minimums.

Q: Is DTF durable?

Q: Do you offer both printing and embroidery on spirit wear?
A: Both. Full-color designs typically run better as screen prints or DTF on tees and hoodies. Chest logos on polos, jackets, and staff apparel look sharper embroidered.

Q: What’s the minimum for a spirit wear run?
A: For screen-printed apparel, 24 pieces per design is our practical minimum. Embroidered spirit wear has no minimum — single-piece orders are fine.

Q: Can you match our school’s colors and mascot?
A: Yes. Send us your logo, mascot art, and color codes (or a photo of an existing shirt) and we’ll match it.

## Work Shirts & Employee Uniforms | Custom Embroidered
URL: https://lakesidethreadz.com/services/work-shirts-uniforms/

Q: Can you embroider hi-vis safety shirts?
A: Yes — we work with ANSI-rated hi-vis shirts and vests. The embroidery doesn't affect the safety rating. Perfect for construction, roadwork, and industrial crews.

Q: What if my employees are different sizes?
A: No problem. Give us a size breakdown with your order and we'll embroider each shirt individually. We can also add individual names to each one.

Q: How durable is embroidery on work shirts?
A: More durable than screen printing or heat transfers. Embroidery is stitched thread — it doesn't peel, crack, or fade. It holds up to industrial washing and daily wear.

Q: Do you offer flame-resistant (FR) work shirts?
A: We can embroider FR shirts you supply. If you need sourcing help, let us know and we'll point you to suppliers who carry FR-rated blanks.

Q: Can you put a logo on the back of work shirts?
A: Absolutely. Back embroidery works great for larger logos. We can also do sleeve embroidery, right chest text, or collar embroidery.

Q: How do I reorder when I hire new employees?
A: We keep your digitized logo on file. Just tell us the sizes and names for new shirts and we'll run them — usually faster than the original order.

Q: Do you offer ANSI safety-rated work shirts?
A: Yes — we can embroider on high-visibility ANSI Class 2 and Class 3 shirts from brands like Berne and Bulwark, plus standard work shirts from Carhartt, Dickies, and Red Kap. Tell us your industry (HVAC, plumbing, oil and gas, construction, marine) and we'll recommend the right blank.

Q: Can you add employee names to work shirts?
A: Yes — individual names add $3 per piece on top of the base embroidery cost. We can do first name, last name, full name, or job title. Send us a list once we confirm the design.
